description: The spec for the spec harness itself. The harness holds its own work to the discipline it enforces on everyone else's: these requirements are the source of truth, the tagged Cucumber scenarios under tests/features are their executable form, and tests/spec_completeness.rs fails the build if the two drift apart. Point the harness at itself with spec --root harness.

requirements.title: Refactoring is refused on a red bar
requirements.story: As a developer held to the discipline by tooling, I want the Red/Green/Refactor phase tracked from the test runs themselves so that a refactor can never begin while the bar is red.
acceptanceCriteria: Given a fresh TDD session, when a failing test run is recorded, then the phase is "RED"
Given a fresh TDD session, when a passing test run is recorded, then the phase is "GREEN"
Given a session whose last run failed, when a refactor is attempted, then the refactor is refused with a message containing "Never refactor on a red bar"
Given a session whose last run passed, when a refactor is started, then the phase is "REFACTOR"

requirements.title: Structural problems in the spec are reported as exact issues
requirements.story: As a developer driving work from a requirements spec, I want structural problems reported as exact, actionable issues so that only a usable spec is ever turned into scenarios and code.
acceptanceCriteria: Given a criterion that names no starting state, action and result, when the spec is validated, then the verdict is "invalid"
Given a well-formed pending requirement, when the spec is validated, then the verdict is "valid"

Given an implemented requirement whose feature file carries none of its tags, when the spec is validated, then an issue reads "REQ-006: no scenario tagged @REQ-006 in features/x.feature - implemented requirements need executable scenarios"
Given two requirements sharing one id, when the spec is validated, then an issue reads "REQ-001: duplicate id - every requirement needs its own"

requirements.title: Vague wording is rejected before any code exists
requirements.story: As a developer agreeing a spec with an agent, I want ambiguous wording called out one finding at a time so that a valid-but-vague requirement is reworded before a single test is generated from it.
acceptanceCriteria: Given a story naming no actor, no benefit and three ambiguous words, when the requirement is refined, then there are 5 findings
Given a story that opens without an actor, when the requirement is refined, then a finding reads "story: missing the actor - start with 'As a ...' so we know who this is for"
Given a story and criteria naming an actor, a benefit, a concrete outcome and an edge case, when the requirement is refined, then the verdict is "clean"
Given a rewording staged but not committed, when the requirement is refined, then the reviewed wording is reported as "staged"

requirements.title: Authored changes are held in staging until a human commits them
requirements.story: As a developer keeping control of every edit an agent proposes, I want authored changes held in a staging area so that nothing reaches the working tree until I have read it as a diff.
acceptanceCriteria: Given a feature file created through staging, when the working tree is read, then the working tree is empty
Given a feature file created through staging, when the staged changes are committed, then the working tree file contains "Feature: Calc"
Given a feature file created through staging, when the staged changes are discarded, then 0 staged changes remain
Given staged content that is not Gherkin, when the staged changes are validated, then the verdict is "invalid"

requirements.title: Each command is offered only the tools that step of the loop needs
requirements.story: As a developer running an LLM-backed command, I want that caller offered a named subset of the tool catalog so that the model stays on task and cannot stage or commit unless the step calls for it.
acceptanceCriteria: Given the default profiles, when every one of them is inspected, then the only caller offered command_run is "implement"
Given the default profiles, when every one of them is inspected, then 0 of them offer a staging or commit tool
Given the caller "spec-draft", when its tools are listed offline, then the offered tools are "list_requirements, get_requirement, validate_spec, refine_requirement"
Given a config naming an invalid tool, when the tools are listed offline, then the offered tools exclude "nope_tool"

requirements.title: Every build tool's report becomes one summary shape
requirements.story: As a developer running the loop in any supported language, I want each build tool's report parsed into a single summary shape so that the RED and GREEN phases are computed the same way everywhere.
acceptanceCriteria: Given cargo test output whose result lines span two binaries, when the output is parsed, then the parsed run has 8 tests, 1 failures, 0 errors, 2 skipped
Given a Surefire report of 3 tests with 1 failure, when the report is parsed, then the parsed run has 3 tests, 1 failures, 0 errors, 1 skipped
Given a build that fails before any test runs, when the output is parsed, then the parsed run has 0 tests, 0 failures, 1 errors, 0 skipped
Given a project whose runtime is absent, when the tests are run, then the run is refused and the refusal names "mvn"

requirements.title: Every next action starts from the spec, not from guesswork
requirements.story: As an agent driving the workflow, I want to list the requirements and read one enriched with its file locations so that the next action is chosen from the catalog rather than from a chat transcript.
acceptanceCriteria: Given a pending requirement and an implemented one, when the requirements are listed, then 2 requirements are listed with their ids, titles and statuses
Given a requirement that lives in an included file, when the requirements are listed, then the listing names that file as its "specFile"
Given a known requirement id, when the requirement is shown, then the reply names its feature file and carries a workflow hint of 1 next step
Given an unknown requirement id, when the requirement is shown, then the reply is an error pointing at list_requirements

requirements.title: A requirement cannot be marked implemented without proof
requirements.story: As a developer who owns the spec wording, I want drafting, status flips and scenario edits staged and gated so that the catalog stays a reviewed source of truth rather than a record of what an agent felt like doing.
acceptanceCriteria: Given a session whose last run failed, when a requirement is marked implemented, then the flip is refused
Given a green bar and a scenario carrying the requirement's tag, when the requirement is marked implemented, then 1 staged change records the feature file
Given a green bar and no scenario carrying the tag, when the requirement is marked implemented, then the flip is refused and the message names the recovery commands
Given a draft the developer declines, when the wizard finishes, then 0 staged changes remain

requirements.title: Generated tests land in staging and fall back to a template
requirements.story: As a developer generating step definitions and unit tests, I want a deterministic template as the floor and model output used only after it validates so that a generation step can degrade but never break the run.
acceptanceCriteria: Given a project with no model resolved, when step definitions are generated, then 1 staged change holds the deterministic template
Given invalid model output, when step definitions are generated, then 1 staged change holds the template rather than the model reply
Given a requirement carrying acceptance criteria, when a unit test is generated, then the staged test fails
Given a feature whose every step is already defined, when step definitions are generated, then the generation is refused

requirements.title: A project's ecosystems are detected and nothing is installed
requirements.story: As a developer pointing the harness at a project, I want its ecosystems detected from marker files and each runtime's presence reported so that execution is attempted only where a runtime already exists.
acceptanceCriteria: Given a project containing "Cargo.toml", when the project is inspected, then the language "Rust" is detected with framework "cucumber-rs" and runtime "cargo"
Given a project containing "pom.xml", when the project is inspected, then the language "Java" is detected with framework "Cucumber-JVM" and runtime "mvn"
Given a project whose runtime is missing, when the project is inspected, then execution is disabled and authoring stays "available"
Given an empty directory, when the project is inspected, then the reply lists 5 supported ecosystems

requirements.title: Undefined steps are found without running anything
requirements.story: As a developer about to scaffold step definitions, I want the steps that have no matching definition found by parsing the sources so that the gap is known without executing or installing anything.
acceptanceCriteria: Given a Java project where one step of three carries a definition, when the missing steps are reported, then 2 steps are missing
Given a Java project whose definitions are written as Cucumber expressions, when the missing steps are reported, then 0 steps are missing
Given a Java project carrying step definitions, when the missing steps are reported, then the report names framework "Cucumber-JVM"

requirements.title: One catalog is the entry point to a backlog spread over many files
requirements.story: As a developer growing a spec beyond one file, I want the root catalog to include child spec files so that the backlog scales while a single entry point still drives the workflow.
acceptanceCriteria: Given a root catalog that includes a child spec file, when the requirements are listed, then 2 requirements merge into one backlog
Given an include naming a file that is absent from disk, when the spec is validated, then the verdict is "invalid"
Given includes that refer back to one another, when the spec is validated, then the cycle is reported as an error
Given a requirement that lives in an included file, when it is marked implemented, then the flip is written back to the file it lives in and 0 other spec files change

requirements.title: A test run narrows to the target that owns the feature
requirements.story: As a developer running one requirement's tests, I want the run narrowed to the test target that owns its feature file so that the bar I am watching is not buried under every other target in the crate.
acceptanceCriteria: Given a crate whose tests directory holds "tdd_state.rs", when the tests are run for feature "tests/features/tdd_state.feature", then the run is scoped to "--test tdd_state"
Given a crate whose tests directory holds only "cucumber.rs", when the tests are run for feature "tests/features/tdd_state.feature", then the run is scoped to "--test cucumber"
Given a crate whose tests directory is missing any target that matches, when the tests are run for that feature, then the run carries no "--test" flag

requirements.title: A drafted requirement carries the prefix its catalog already uses
requirements.story: As a developer drafting into a spec that already numbers its requirements, I want the new id to carry the prefix the catalog uses so that one binary serves every spec without being told how each one numbers.
acceptanceCriteria: Given a catalog whose highest id is "HARNESS-014", when a requirement is drafted, then the staged id is "HARNESS-015"
Given an empty catalog holding 0 requirements, when a requirement is drafted, then the staged id is "REQ-001"
Given a catalog whose highest id is "REQ-0007", when a requirement is drafted, then the staged id is "REQ-0008"
Given a catalog numbering "HARNESS-001" that also includes a file numbering "CLI-099", when a requirement is drafted, then the staged id is "HARNESS-002"
Given a catalog whose highest id is "HARNESS-014", when the status is reported, then the next id is "HARNESS-015"
Given a catalog holding "HARNESS-014", when the delivery target "harness-014" is read, then the target is requirement "HARNESS-014"

requirements.title: The project is found by walking up from the working directory
requirements.story: As a developer running spec from inside a repository, I want the nearest enclosing project used when none is named so that the command works on what I am looking at without a flag.
acceptanceCriteria: Given a project whose catalog sits at its root, when the root is discovered from "src/domain" inside it, then the reported root is the directory holding "requirements/requirements.json"
Given a project nested inside another project, when the root is discovered from "harness/src", then the reported root is "harness"
Given a directory holding ".spec" and no catalog, when the root is discovered from "src" inside it, then the reported root is the directory holding ".spec"
Given a directory that is itself the project root, when the root is discovered from it, then 0 roots are reported
Given a directory whose every ancestor is missing both markers, when the root is discovered from it, then 0 roots are reported

requirements.title: An undirected draft lands in the catalog file covering the working directory
requirements.story: As a developer drafting in a catalog split across files, I want a requirement to land in the spec file covering the directory I am in so that the backlog stays organised without my naming a file every time.
acceptanceCriteria: Given a catalog including "core/math.json" and a command run in "core", when a requirement is drafted with no file named, then "requirements/core/math.json" holds 2 requirements
Given a command run in "src/domain", for which a covering spec file is missing, when a requirement is drafted with no file named, then "requirements/requirements.json" holds 2 requirements
Given a catalog including "core/math.json" and a command run in "core", when a requirement is drafted naming "requirements/requirements.json", then the staged id is "REQ-002"
